title: Join the Ropes at the Smallest Cost

concept.title: Always join the two shortest ropes (the greedy choice behind Huffman coding)
body: Joining two ropes of lengths `x` and `y` costs `x + y` and gives one rope of length `x + y`. To join all ropes into one at the **smallest total cost**, always join the **two shortest** ropes. The reason: a rope that is joined early is counted again in every later join that contains it, so the ropes that are joined first should be the short ones, and the long ones should be joined last, counted only a few times.
A **min-heap** gives the two shortest ropes, and the new rope goes back into the heap, because it may again be among the shortest.

body.code:
import heapq
heap = list(ropes)
heapq.heapify(heap)
total = 0
while len(heap) > 1:
    joined = heapq.heappop(heap) + heapq.heappop(heap)
    total += joined
    heapq.heappush(heap, joined)
print(total)

body: The same greedy builds the *Huffman code*, which gives frequent letters short codes in file compression: there the "ropes" are letter frequencies. The total cost can be large: 20000 ropes of 10^9 cost about 3 * 10^14, so use 64-bit numbers.

statement: There are `n` ropes with the given lengths. Joining two ropes costs the sum of their lengths and produces one rope. Join all the ropes into one rope, and print the smallest possible total cost (0 if there is only one rope).
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers: the lengths of the ropes.

examples.note: Join 2 and 3 (cost 5), then 4 and 5 (cost 9), then 6 and 9 (cost 15): 5 + 9 + 15 = 29.

hints: Join the two shortest ropes first.
Use a min-heap: take two ropes, add the cost, and push the joined rope back.

explanation: A min-heap gives the two shortest ropes; their sum is added to the cost and pushed back as a new rope, until one rope remains.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
heap = list(a)
heapq.heapify(heap)
total = 0
while len(heap) > 1:
    joined = heapq.heappop(heap) + heapq.heappop(heap)
    total += joined
    heapq.heappush(heap, joined)
print(total)
